narration: We begin with an empty canvas. The figure is built from three stages; the first, outlined in blue, is where the pipeline starts.
Stage one is 3D head geometry learning: it recovers the shape and pose of the head from the reference video.
Its input is S-ref, a stack of reference frames showing the same person from slightly different viewpoints.
A head extraction step crops and masks each frame, producing X-ref, the clean head region without background.
X-ref is fed to two networks in parallel: a Depth Net that predicts geometry, and a Pose Net that predicts camera pose.
Depth Net outputs a depth map, Pose Net outputs per-frame rotations and translations, and together they drive the flow computation.
That geometry feeds the second stage, outlined in pink, directly below.
Stage two is recurrent canonical head generation: it fuses all reference frames into one canonical representation.
An encoder embeds X-ref, and the computed flow warps those features into the shared canonical view.
A ConvLSTM accumulates the warped features across frames into the hidden canonical state h-c, which a decoder turns into the canonical head x-hat-c.
The third stage, outlined in orange, occupies the right of the figure.
Stage three is the attention-based fusion mechanism, which renders the final driven frame.
It takes the canonical head x-hat-c, the driving frame s-dri with its pose, and the reference frame s-ref; the transform block re-poses the canonical head.
In the top branch, the re-posed head x-hat-dri is encoded and warped by its own flow, then gated by an attention mask.
A flow and attention map predictor produces both the flow fields and the attention maps that weight each branch.
In the bottom branch, s-ref is encoded and warped the same way; the two gated streams are summed and decoded into the final driven image s-hat-dri.
